perQuery.note: A has both landmarks (PARTNER 3 #1 and Evolut 6-year #2) with clean metadata, while B contains the Evolut 6-year paper but omits PARTNER 3 and mixes in a minimally-invasive-surgery item.
Both place the exact DAPA-HF paper at #1, but A's supporting list is cleaner whereas B includes a correction notice, missing-id entries, and lower-quality summaries.
Both have CLARITY-AD at #1; A's top items are tightly focused on lecanemab efficacy/reviews while B drifts into tangential neuroinflammation and non-cognitive-symptom items despite good recency.
B's list stays squarely on SGLT2i CV-outcome/mortality meta-analyses matching the PICO, whereas A drifts toward CKD/renal and single-drug HF papers less aligned to the CV-mortality outcome.
B surfaces the current 2024 ESC AF guideline and the 2020 ESC guideline high, while A leads with the older 2016/2010 versions and never reaches the 2024 primary document near the top.
A leads with strong network meta-analyses and is clean throughout, while B opens with a dubious low-tier journal entry and includes a duplicate BMJ pair and a no-id item.

Both retrieve the RECOVERY dexamethasone NEJM paper and medRxiv preprint, but A's top results are the definitive primary papers whereas B fills the list with Twitter journal-club, news, and commentary items.
Both put KEYNOTE-189 primary paper at #1; B's supporting list is more relevant (5-year outcomes, PROs, updates) while A includes a no-id formulary entry and a low-tier journal item.
Both resolve DAPA-HF well, but B includes the primary NEJM DAPA-HF results paper (PMID:31535829) while A surfaces only design/substudy papers without the primary results article.

A resolves PARTNER 3 to the correct balloon-expandable TAVR RCT (though with two unrelated PRO/advance-care-planning items) whereas B catastrophically returns the HIV PARTNER study, missing the cardiac trial almost entirely.
A is entirely on-target with KEYNOTE-189 analyses and follow-ups, while B mixes in unrelated KEYNOTE-590/789/859/495 trials and a press release, diluting relevance.

Both include the 2021 SPRINT final report, but B ranks it #1 with the SPRINT design paper #2 while A buries the final report at #7 and leads with a recurrent-stroke trial; neither lists the original 2015 NEJM SPRINT.
B leads with high-yield JAMA/Lancet HFrEF reviews and management syntheses, while A includes several tangential renal-dialysis and AF-overlap papers reducing top-10 relevance.
B surfaces the authoritative 2019 ATS/IDSA CAP guideline plus key RCTs/SRs, whereas A relies heavily on older AFP review articles and has several no-id entries without reaching the primary guideline.
A includes the landmark DOAC RCTs (ROCKET-AF, ARISTOTLE), the ESC guideline, and a current review, while B offers mostly older/generic narrative reviews and lacks the landmark trials.
Both retrieve ProCESS/ARISE/ProMISe and the PRISM patient-level meta-analysis, but A ranks the definitive 2017 NEJM meta-analysis #1 whereas B leads with a CJEM summary above the primary trials.
Both lead with the Oxygen-ICU RCT and include IOTA/ICU-ROX-era evidence; A has a couple of weak low-tier entries while B includes some tangential ECMO/cardiac-arrest subsets, roughly balancing out.

B anchors on the landmark SELECT trial plus SOUL/SURMOUNT-5 follow-ups directly answering semaglutide CV outcomes, while A returns mostly 2026 network meta-analyses that are recent but miss the primary CVOT evidence.
B's list is more on-topic and current for CAR-T in myeloma (2024 updates, reviews), whereas A drifts into lymphoma, microRNA, and immuno-oncology items less specific to myeloma CAR-T.
A delivers strong recent SR/MAs/NMAs plus the Cochrane review with clean metadata, while B includes older meta-analyses, a no-id Cochrane entry, and a non-systematic opinion piece.
A leads with the high-impact Lancet five-RCT meta-analysis and EClinicalMedicine HF-hospitalization SR, while B's pooled analyses are relevant but lower-impact and include a generic Cureus entry.
Both retrieve the Cochrane reviews (CD002243) and major SR/MAs; A is marginally cleaner while B includes a protocol and a commentary, but both answer the Cochrane intent well.
B ranks the current 2020 ACC/AHA VHD guideline high with the 2017 focused update, while A leads with 2014-version duplicates including one malformed PMID (URL-in-PMID field).

A ranks the KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline and its executive summary at #1-2 but includes a no-id PDF and off-topic ADPKD/anemia guidelines; B leads with a KDOQI commentary above the primary KDIGO document and has several no-id entries.
A includes the STAMPEDE 5-year NEJM trial and long-term cohort/meta-analyses with strong ranking, while B is dominated by older meta-analyses and symposium summaries and omits the key STAMPEDE RCT.

A leads with the Lancet individual-patient-data meta-analysis plus 10-year SYNTAX/PRECOMBAT data, while B includes a malformed NEJM 'correction' entry and stays more at the 5-year horizon than the requested ten-year outcomes.

Both retrieve the DAPA-CKD NEJM trial and prespecified analyses, but A ranks the primary trial #3 with consistently relevant items whereas B places it #1 yet includes an off-topic arthritis/CBT entry, hurting trust.

Both give strong cohort/population evidence quantifying post-mRNA myocarditis in young males; A is slightly better targeted to the young-male systematic review and large cohorts, while B is also excellent with the Nordic and Israeli cohorts.

A is tightly focused on GLP-1 and acute pancreatitis risk across RCT/observational evidence, while B leads with broad CV/kidney-outcome meta-analyses only tangentially addressing the pancreatitis safety question.

B leads with the pivotal NEJM DKA-after-SGLT2-initiation cohort and on-topic DKA studies, while A opens with a generic CV-outcomes meta-analysis; B is marred by one clearly irrelevant urothelial-carcinoma entry but is more on-target overall.

Both lead with the seminal JAMA-IM cohort/BMJ nationwide study and a strong set of SR/MAs and cohorts; B usefully adds a negative/null EHJ study while A is uniformly on-target, leaving them effectively equal.

Both include the SURMOUNT-5 head-to-head NEJM trial and the JAMA-IM comparative study; A pairs them with high-impact NMAs and the SURPASS-2 RCT, while B leans on several lower-tier Cureus/regional-journal meta-analyses.

Both place the PLATO NEJM trial #1 with the PLATO invasive-strategy Lancet paper; B's supporting set (POPular AGE, PLATO substudies, registries, RCTs) is clean while A includes two malformed PMID (URL-in-field) entries.

B is uniformly focused on mechanistic/translational SGLT2i cardioprotection reviews, whereas A mixes in tangential network-meta-analyses on dementia, sex differences, and anticancer effects diluting the mechanism intent.

overall.summary: Engine A wins the majority of queries, driven by superior landmark recall on acronym/exact-paper and long-term-outcome queries (notably resolving PARTNER 3 to the correct cardiac trial where B returned the HIV PARTNER study, and surfacing landmark DOAC and bariatric/STAMPEDE RCTs B missed) and cleaner metadata with fewer junk entries. Engine B is stronger on recency-sensitive and guideline-current queries (2024 ESC AF, current ACC/AHA VHD, SELECT/semaglutide, SGLT2-DKA and mechanism), where it favors newer or more on-topic evidence. Overall A edges B on recall, ranking, and trust across the 30-query set, with several ties on safety queries where both performed excellently.
